text: Accounts on a server: sign-up as an option, automatic login with a browser key, upgrade to a permanent login
description:
Felix 2026-11-12: we do implement a user system. Accounts belong to the server. Whoever runs a server configures accounts; local hosting keeps today's default, a super user without login.

Ways to get an account, each a server option:
- "Anyone can create an account".
- Automatic: login happens with a key created in the browser's local storage; an exclamation mark recommends upgrading to a permanent login. This is what Commons Hub and Hack the Hub use, because onboarding has to be as easy as possible.
- Invitation links: permanent ones (maybe limited in time) and ones redeemable once. To be implemented, but not used for Commons Hub; they are there to switch to if open sign-up causes problems.

Permanent logins, decided by Felix 2026-11-12:
- user name and password
- crypto wallet, fully self-hosted: start with EIP-6963 (finding the wallets in the browser), EIP-1193 (talking to a wallet) and Sign-In with Ethereum, then add direct mobile integrations selectively. No external accounts, API keys, hosted authentication or third-party servers; the server owns the entire authentication process.
- email only optional, later: setting up a mail server is a burden

Carried over from fcb38df6 (Felix 2026-11-11): non-human agents get a user identity too and are shown on the ideas they work on while they work. How an MCP client connects is idea "Connect an MCP client through an authentication workflow".

Today: accounts with name, role and password hash in .bowman/runtime/accounts.json, created by the admin on the command line (accounts.ts); no sign-up, no key login, no invitations.

Assumed by Claude: the browser key is a key pair, the server stores the public key and the name, and login is a signature; without an upgrade, clearing the browser data loses the account.

status.comment: Planned 2026-11-12 at Felix's request; kinds of login and the wallet approach decided the same day; nothing built.
